title: Fault-Tolerant Deep Learning Cache with Hash Ring for Load Balancing in HPC Systems
problem: Large-scale deep learning on HPC systems uses distributed node-local caching but lacks fault tolerance; analysis of Frontier SLURM logs shows over 30% of jobs fail after an average of 75 minutes, jeopardizing training completion.
motivation: Fault tolerance in distributed caching is critical for large-scale deep learning on HPC systems to prevent catastrophic job failures and training time losses from node failures.
method: The paper proposes fault-tolerance strategies that use a hash ring technique to recache data lost from failed nodes with balanced redistribution across remaining nodes in a distributed node-local caching system. The hash ring mechanism intelligently redirects cached data to operational nodes rather than falling back to the parallel file system (PFS), reducing I/O bottlenecks.
key_novelty: Hash ring-based balanced recaching of data lost from failed nodes in distributed node-local caching systems to minimize PFS reliance.
contributions: Analysis of 6 months of SLURM job logs revealing 30% failure rate on Frontier supercomputer
Hash ring-based fault-tolerance strategy for distributed node-local caching with load balancing
Demonstrates 25% training time reduction versus PFS redirection approach on Frontier
Effective load balancing of training data redistribution across operational nodes
limitations: Evaluation limited to Frontier; generalizability to other HPC systems and performance at extreme scale not discussed.
primary_theme: Fault-tolerant distributed caching with hash ring load balancing
